prose_updates.tldr: As an exact-real statistical procedure on the declared linear Gaussian variance-reset class, the certificate returns the environment-labelled transitive closure \(I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I\) and an environment-indexed encoder estimate within \(\tau\) of the parent-supported population range class, or abstains. Its per-environment sample bound is quadratic in \(1/\tau\) and essentially linear in \(\log(1/\alpha)\), up to displayed logarithms. Separately, rational post-summary rank, repeated-eigenspace, projector-product, and singular-value decisions admit a proved polynomial-bit implementation with an explicit aggregate rounding budget. The encoder output is neither asserted invertible nor a unique representative of a repeated positive eigenspace. A legal all-dimension Gaussian family has constant reached gaps but exponentially small unqueried equation-(22) margin, showing that the published global margin is not necessary for recoverability, without extending the positive Gaussian theorem to the full published class.

project_justification.fill: The project supplies an anytime-valid exact-real Gaussian recover-or-abstain certificate with public reached gaps, a sharper cap \(B_{\mathrm{samp}}<66q_{\star}u_{\star}\), environment-labelled graph and encoder targets, and explicit encoder error bars. The resulting per-environment dependence is quadratic in \(1/\tau\) and essentially linear in \(\log(1/\alpha)\), rather than the anchor paper's RKHS fourth-power accuracy dependence. It also supplies a deterministic polynomial-bit post-summary realization with total arithmetic enclosure error at most \(e_{\star}/4\). The positive theorem remains confined to the Gaussian variance-reset subclass; the all-dimension family establishes over the broader published class only that equation \(22\) is not necessary.

prose_updates.related_work: Acartürk et al. (2024) are the strict finite-sample comparator. Their Section 5 equation (22) takes a positive-eigenvalue minimum over all subset sums, while printed equation (23) and Lemma 10 identify a projector-product quantity with \(\min_i\|H_{i,:}\|_2\|G_{:,i}\|_2\). The latter norm product is at least one by biorthogonality even though a projector-product norm is at most one, so the present proofs use the actual subspaces and the valid reciprocal witness bound \(\rho_i(G)\), never the printed identity. The positive certificate is a covariance-specialized result for the linear Gaussian perfect variance-reset subclass and is not a strengthening on the source's full smooth soft-intervention class. The explicit Gaussian family is nevertheless legal in that published class and satisfies Assumption 1 and its other non-margin conditions; its recovery with exponentially small off-transcript \(\eta^{\ast}(P)\) shows only that equation (22) is not necessary. The Gaussian rate has quadratic \(1/\tau\) and essentially linear \(\log(1/\alpha)\) dependence, whereas the anchor's RKHS analysis has fourth-power accuracy dependence. Sobczyk (2025), Corollary 4.5 of arXiv version 2, supplies the deterministic certified spectral-projector primitive; the present theorem adapts it to the zero/positive cluster gap, adds exact rational inertia for rank and projector-product singular-value tests, and budgets their composed error along the adaptive transcript. Varıcı et al. (2025) provide the population score-range program, and Squires et al. (2023) validate the legal linear intervention substrate.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The numerical theorem is a post-summary result: it assumes outward rational enclosures of the exact fixed-coordinate empirical covariance summaries and, for a rational ambient encoder, a supplied enclosure of the canonical support frame. Processing raw observations additionally incurs their representation, reading, and covariance-formation cost, including at least \(\Omega(B_{\mathrm{tot}})\) record operations. The statistical theorem remains exact-real at the sampling layer. Its encoder guarantee is distance to a unit-row parent-supported range class, not invertibility, a unique repeated-eigenspace representative, or latent-coordinate error independent of the mixing map. The positive guarantee is specific to Gaussian variance resets and does not transfer to the full published soft-intervention class.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The positive statistical and polynomial-bit post-summary theorems concern the linear Gaussian perfect variance-reset subclass in fixed coordinates on \(\mathcal S\). They target only \(I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I\) and the correspondingly environment-indexed parent-supported encoder range class. The rational algorithm is polynomial after covariance summaries are available; an end-to-end raw-data implementation must also pay at least \(\Omega(B_{\mathrm{tot}})\) to read the sample records, so its runtime is not polynomial only in logarithmic gap parameters. The separation family is legal in Acartürk et al.'s broader smooth soft-intervention class and proves that equation (22)'s all-subset margin is not necessary for recovery there, but it does not promote the Gaussian certificate to that broader class. Actual projector geometry and \(\rho_i(G)\) replace the source's false printed norm-product identity. Neither an invertible encoder nor a canonical representative inside a repeated positive eigenspace is claimed.
